dedupe_keys.name: experimental investigation of the effect of wake steering on the noise emission of a commercial wind turbine

description: FINEZ, Arthur and colleagues describe this resource in the native deposit. Twenty-four ground microphones encircle a commercial 2.2 MW turbine at tip-height distance, providing fifteen-degree angular coverage. Nacelle and ground lidar characterize inflow while yaw offsets range from minus twenty to plus twenty degrees. The source reports asymmetric directivity and a modest sound-power change under yaw control. An earlier conference description of the same microphone-circle experiment is grouped with its distinct numerical findings preserved. The case informs noise-aware farm control, not a claim of unchanged acoustic impact. Zenodo provides the deposit with open access under cc-by-4.0. This record represents the documented application and its stated scope. Publication access does not imply that its underlying measurements or implementation are public. Coverage is limited to the stated experiment, model or application; transfer to other turbines, sites or operating regimes requires separate assessment. Publication date alone does not establish current maintenance. The observations provide a reference case for noise-aware wind-farm control.
